construct: In a crossover trial each participant receives multiple interventions in sequence. If the effect of the first intervention persists into the next treatment period, an inadequate washout allows residual treatment effect to contaminate the second-period outcome, producing a carryover effect.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: In a two-period crossover trial with long-lasting treatments and no washout, residual pharmacodynamic effect from period 1 can contaminate period 2; this is a carryover effect.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Lead-time, recall, ecological, and verification biases describe unrelated study-design problems and do not involve persistence of a prior intervention across crossover periods.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The stem explicitly states both prolonged post-discontinuation effect and absent washout, making carryover—not generic period/order effects—the direct methodological defect.
